terms.definition: A device that opens or closes the current path — the circuit's gate.
terms.function: One click decides whether current has a road.
terms.whereItIs: The rocker lever on the switch body.
terms.whyItMatters: Every wall plate, button, and breaker runs on this idea.

terms.definition: Closed = contacts touch, loop complete; open = gap, loop broken.
terms.whyItMatters: It's the on/off semantics of every circuit.
terms.whereItIs: The contact posts touching or parted.

terms.definition: An open switch halts current everywhere in a series loop at once.
terms.whyItMatters: Why breakers can trip out danger in an instant.
terms.whereItIs: The bulb and ammeter zeroing simultaneously.

terms.definition: The maximum amps a switch is built to carry safely.
terms.whyItMatters: Oversized current overheats and ruins any switch.
terms.whereItIs: The post-warming warning under high ammeter.
